problems.claim: WTP: 'Anchore $34,500/yr per host on AWS Marketplace ... GitHub exports SBOMs on its free dependency graph'
problems.issue: The AWS Marketplace listing prices 'Anchore Enterprise Cloud Image' at $34,500 per 12 months as one flat dimension: 'a single host Anchore Enterprise deployment'. That is a flat price for a single-host deployment, not a per-host rate. The cited GitHub docs page explains how to export an SBOM from the dependency graph but never says the feature is free or which plans include it, so 'free dependency graph' is not supported by the cited source.

problems.claim: Snyk Open Source pricing: 'Free tier; Team $25/contributing dev/month, 5-dev minimum, up to 10 contributing devs; Enterprise custom' (source: snyk.io/start/team)
problems.issue: The page supports the Free plan, $25 per contributing developer/month, the 5-developer minimum and the 10-developer cap ($1,375 annually). It says nothing about an Enterprise plan or custom pricing, so 'Enterprise custom' is not supported by this source.

problems.claim: GitHub Code Security (Dependabot): 'Dependabot alerts/updates plus premium dependency review bundled into GitHub'; pricing 'Code Security $30/active committer/month; basic Dependabot included with GitHub'
problems.issue: The changelog confirms $30 per month per active committer and says GitHub Team organizations can now buy Code Security, which includes 'Dependabot features'. It never says basic Dependabot is included free with GitHub, and it does not mention 'premium dependency review'. Both statements are unsupported by the cited source. The post is also specifically about GitHub Team plan customers, not SMB to enterprise generally.

problems.claim: WTP: 'Buyers pay, but switch on price, and free Dependabot sets a low baseline.'
problems.issue: None of the three wtp_sources (snyk.io/start/team, the GitHub changelog, mend.io/pricing) shows buyers switching on price, and none says Dependabot is free. The Snyk $25 and GitHub $30 prices and Mend's per-contributing-developer pricing with no list price are supported. The switching and free-Dependabot conclusions are not.

problems.claim: WorkOS pricing: 'Per connection: $125/mo for connections 1-15, falling to $65 at 51-100; SSO and SCIM billed as separate connections' (source: workos.com/pricing)
problems.issue: The page lists '$125 / ea' (1-15) down to '$65 / ea' (51-100) under both Single Sign-On and Directory Sync. It never states a monthly billing period for connections; '/mo' appears only for other items such as Audit Logs and Radar. The FAQ says 'Each enterprise customer you support with SSO or Directory Sync is counted as one connection', which does not clearly say SSO and SCIM are billed as separate connections and can be read as the opposite. Separate price tables imply separate billing, but the page never states it.

problems.claim: WTP: IT buyers '... resent the SSO/SCIM tax.'
problems.issue: The cited wtp_sources (Stytch pricing, Stytch AWS Marketplace listing, Okta pricing) support the prices: Stytch 5 free connections then $125 per connection; a $25,000/12-month Stytch Platform contract; Okta Core Essentials $14 and Essentials $17, billed annually with a $1,500 minimum; Lifecycle Management an add-on on Starter. None of them shows buyer resentment of an 'SSO/SCIM tax'. That part is unsupported by the WTP sources.

problems.claim: Teleport pricing: 'not public (quote-based; usage-based on monthly active users and Teleport Protected Resources, with each tbot machine-identity instance counted as a TPR ...)'; segment 'mid-market / enterprise' (source: Teleport_Pricing_Guide_Rev_June_16_2026 PDF)
problems.issue: The PDF supports MAU and TPR usage-based metrics and 'We count each unique instance of tbot as a TPR'. It publishes no prices but never says pricing is quote-based or names a sales contact, and it says nothing about mid-market buyers; it covers only the 'Enterprise Edition'. 'Quote-based' and 'mid-market' are inferences, not statements from the source. The gapfinder fetch of the PDF failed; it was read after downloading it with curl.

problems.claim: Cribl Stream pricing: 'Cribl.Cloud free up to 1 TB/day; paid Stream ingest credits ~$0.27/GB (Standard, up to 5 TB/day) to $0.32/GB (Enterprise), $1 per credit, plus worker infrastructure' (source: cribl.io/pricing)
problems.issue: Neither the fetched page text nor the raw HTML of cribl.io/pricing contains a $0.27/GB or $0.32/GB rate. The only per-GB figures are static-egress charges of 0.06-0.12 credits/GB. The rendered fetch timed out, and WebFetch cannot resolve cribl.io in this session. The page does support $1 = 1 credit, Standard up to 5TB/day, a Free plan up to 1TB/day, Stream priced 'based on GBs of data ingested' and an extra managed-infrastructure fee. However, it qualifies the 1TB/day free figure with '* See Cribl.Cloud section for data limits and availability in cloud', so 'Cribl.Cloud free up to 1 TB/day' is not shown. The segment 'enterprise / large SOC' is also not stated.

problems.claim: WTP: 'Enterprises pay per-GB pipeline fees (Cribl.Cloud ~$0.27-0.32/GB in credits above a free tier of up to 1 TB/day)'
problems.issue: The only support for a per-GB price is one PeerSpot reviewer's estimate ('approximately $0.32 per GB for ST enterprise estimate'). No cited source shows $0.27/GB, and cribl.io/pricing shows no per-GB ingest rate (see the Cribl vendor row). The rest checks out: the CrowdStrike release confirms it agreed to acquire Onum; PeerSpot reviewers call Cribl 'costly as it scales with data volumes', ask for 'Better options based on user base, enterprise size, or data volume', and one says 'at a small level, the pricing is good'.

problems.claim: WTP: 'HCP Vault Dedicated ~$112.17/client/month (Standard, official price list)' (source: hashicorp.com/pricing/all)
problems.issue: Unverified: the source could not be read. gapfinder fetch returned HTTP 429. fetch --render returned a bot challenge page ('Failed to verify your browser, Code 21'). WebFetch returned HTTP 404 for both hashicorp.com/pricing/all and www.hashicorp.com/en/pricing/all. No figure, tier or unit could be checked. The other WTP figures are confirmed: Aembit Teams from $20/workload/month and Cyera Identity (Oasis) Starter Pack $100,000 per 12 months.

problems.claim: Interlynk pricing: 'free Community tier; AWS Marketplace 12-month SaaS contracts by active developers: $18,000 (10), $36,000 (25), $60,000 (50), $100,000 (100)'; segment 'SMB to enterprise, device makers'
problems.issue: The listing confirms the four 12-month prices, which are for a product named 'AWS SBOM Manager (SaaS)'. It mentions only a 'free trial', not a free Community tier, so the free tier is unsupported. On buyers, the listing names medical device manufacturers, connected-device and firmware teams, AI providers and '100+ regulated companies'. It says nothing about SMBs.

problems.claim: WTP: 'Manifest signed a three-year device-maker deal (value undisclosed)' (wtp_source: commission.europa.eu Cyber Resilience Act news, 2026-09-11)
problems.issue: The cited European Commission page covers only CRA reporting obligations, which start 11 Sep 2026, with main obligations from 11 Dec 2027. It never mentions Manifest or any deal. The Manifest deal is supported only by the PR Newswire release in the vendor row (a three-year SaaS agreement with a publicly traded medical device maker, May 2024, value not disclosed), which is not among the wtp_sources. The cited WTP source does not support this claim.
